description: God told His people to remember for centuries. Then He said forget all that. What I am about to do is bigger. And it was.
excerpt: Throughout the whole Old Testament, God keeps telling His people to remember. And then here in Isaiah, He says something almost the opposite. Forget all that. It is nothing compared to what I am going to do.
verse: "But forget all that—it is nothing compared to what I am going to do."
body_html:
Throughout the whole Old Testament, God keeps telling His people to remember. Remember what I did in Egypt. Remember how I brought you out. Remember the miracles. Remember my faithfulness. Remember, remember, remember.

And then here in Isaiah, He says something almost the opposite.

Forget all that. It is nothing compared to what I am going to do.

The bigger context makes it even better. He is talking about the exodus. The parting of the Red Sea. The defeat of Pharaoh's army. The rescue that shaped the entire identity of Israel. That was the defining miracle in their history. And God is saying, that was amazing, but you have not seen anything yet. What I am about to do will be even bigger.

What an exciting thought.

Because if the exodus was the small version, what is the big version? What could possibly be greater than that?

Looking back now, we know. Jesus. The rescue from sin and death that reaches every person on earth who will receive it. The exodus was a shadow. Jesus was the substance. The Red Sea being parted was incredible. But an empty tomb was greater.

And I think this verse still applies to us today.

God is not done. He is still doing new things. The best of what He has planned is still ahead. However amazing what He has done in your past has been, it does not compare to what He is still going to do.

That is worth waking up to.

We can get so focused on the story we already know that we miss the one He is currently writing. We can spend so much time celebrating what He did that we do not have eyes for what He is doing. God is not looking backward. He is always working forward. And He invites us to have hearts that are ready to see it.

What if the best chapter of your walk with God is still coming?

What if what He has done for you so far is just the beginning?
question: Where in your life have you been so focused on what God did that you have missed what He is doing right now?
